title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port -1
proposed_fix: Replace the all-protocol ingress rule with least-privilege rules, e.g. ingress { from_port=443; to_port=443; protocol="tcp"; cidr_blocks=[var.trusted_cidr]; description="HTTPS from trusted CIDR" }.
justification: AWS security groups should grant least privilege; removing protocol -1 and 0.0.0.0/0 prevents unrestricted inbound access. See AWS VPC security group rules documentation.

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 3389
proposed_fix: Remove public RDP ingress; if RDP is required, use ingress { from_port=3389; to_port=3389; protocol="tcp"; cidr_blocks=[var.admin_cidr]; description="RDP from admin CIDR" }.
justification: Exposing RDP to the internet enables brute-force and exploitation. Restrict to trusted admin CIDRs per AWS security group best practices.

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 22
proposed_fix: Remove public SSH ingress; if SSH is required, use ingress { from_port=22; to_port=22; protocol="tcp"; cidr_blocks=[var.admin_cidr]; description="SSH from admin CIDR" }.
justification: Internet-exposed SSH increases attack surface. Restrict to trusted CIDRs per AWS security group best practices.

title: Ensure no security groups allow egress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port -1
proposed_fix: Replace unrestricted egress with specific egress rules, e.g. egress { from_port=443; to_port=443; protocol="tcp"; cidr_blocks=[var.allowed_egress_cidr]; description="HTTPS egress" }.
justification: Restricting egress reduces data exfiltration and lateral movement. See AWS security group egress rule guidance.

title: Ensure every security group and rule has a description
proposed_fix: Add description to each ingress and egress block, e.g. description="HTTPS from trusted CIDR" and description="HTTPS egress to approved services".
justification: Descriptions improve auditability and incident response. AWS security group rules support and recommend descriptions.

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 80
proposed_fix: Remove public HTTP ingress; if HTTP is required, use ingress { from_port=80; to_port=80; protocol="tcp"; cidr_blocks=[var.trusted_cidr]; description="HTTP from trusted CIDR" } or redirect to HTTPS.
justification: Public HTTP exposes unencrypted traffic. Restrict or redirect per AWS security group best practices.

title: Ensure IAM policies does not allow data exfiltration
proposed_fix: Replace Action="*" and Resource="*" with explicit read actions/resources and add Condition constraints, e.g. Action=["s3:GetObject"], Resource=["arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec/*"], Condition={StringEquals={"aws:PrincipalTag/team"="app"}}.
justification: Wildcard IAM permissions allow broad data access. Scope actions/resources and add conditions per AWS IAM least privilege guidance.

title: Ensure IAM policies does not allow privilege escalation
proposed_fix: Remove iam:*, sts:AssumeRole, and other escalation-capable actions from the policy; grant only required actions on specific resources, e.g. Action=["s3:GetObject"], Resource=["arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec/*"].
justification: IAM wildcards can enable privilege escalation. Use least privilege and avoid self-modifying IAM permissions per AWS IAM best practices.

title: Ensure IAM policies does not allow credentials exposure
proposed_fix: Remove actions like iam:Get*, iam:List*, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, and ssm:GetParameter unless required; replace Action="*" Resource="*" with explicit scoped actions/resources.
justification: Broad read permissions can expose credentials and secrets. Scope to required secrets and resources per AWS IAM least privilege guidance.

title: Ensure IAM policies does not allow permissions management / resource exposure without constraints
proposed_fix: Remove permissions-management actions such as iam:Attach*, iam:Put*, iam:Create*, and iam:PassRole; grant only required actions on specific resources and add Condition constraints.
justification: Permissions-management wildcards can alter access controls. AWS recommends least privilege and explicit resource scoping for IAM policies.

title: Ensure IAM policies does not allow write access without constraints
proposed_fix: Replace Action="*" Resource="*" with explicit write actions and resources, e.g. Action=["s3:PutObject"], Resource=["arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec/*"], and add Condition constraints.
justification: Unconstrained write access can modify or destroy resources. Scope write permissions per AWS IAM least privilege guidance.

title: Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*-*" administrative privileges are not created
proposed_fix: Replace the admin policy statement with least-privilege statements: remove Action="*" and Resource="*", list only required actions and ARNs, and add conditions where possible.
justification: Full administrative privileges violate least privilege. See AWS IAM policy best practices and Checkov CKV_AWS_62 guidance.

title: Ensure no IAM policies documents allow "*" as a statement's actions
proposed_fix: Change Action="*" to explicit actions, e.g. Action=["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket"], and scope Resource to required ARNs.
justification: Wildcard actions grant excessive permissions. Use explicit actions per AWS IAM least privilege guidance.

title: Ensure no IAM policies documents allow "*" as a statement's resource for restrictable actions
proposed_fix: Replace Resource="*" with specific ARNs, e.g. Resource=["arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec","arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec/*"].
justification: Restrictable actions should be limited to required resources. See AWS IAM resource-level permissions documentation.

title: Ensure that S3 bucket has a Public Access block
proposed_fix: Add resource aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block "public_assets" { bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id; block_public_acls=true; block_public_policy=true; ignore_public_acls=true; restrict_public_buckets=true }.
justification: S3 Block Public Access prevents accidental public exposure. See AWS S3 Block Public Access documentation.

title: Ensure S3 buckets should have event notifications enabled
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_notification with bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id and a target event, e.g. lambda_function { lambda_function_arn=var.notification_lambda_arn; events=["s3:ObjectCreated:*"] }.
justification: Event notifications improve monitoring and response to bucket changes. See AWS S3 event notification documentation.

title: Ensure that Security Groups are attached to another resource
proposed_fix: Attach aws_security_group.open_sg to an approved resource, e.g. add vpc_security_group_ids=[aws_security_group.open_sg.id] to the relevant aws_instance, ENI, or load balancer.
justification: Unattached security groups provide no protection and may indicate drift. AWS recommends associating security groups with resources.

title: S3 Bucket has an ACL defined which allows public READ access.
proposed_fix: Change acl="public-read" to acl="private" or remove the ACL line; serve public content via CloudFront/OAC or a scoped bucket policy instead.
justification: Public-read ACLs expose objects directly. AWS recommends disabling ACLs and using bucket policies/CloudFront for controlled access.

title: Ensure that S3 buckets are encrypted with KMS by default
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration with bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id and rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm="aws:kms" } }.
justification: Default KMS encryption protects data at rest with customer-managed keys. See AWS S3 default encryption documentation.

title: Ensure that S3 bucket has cross-region replication enabled
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration with role=aws_iam_role.replication.arn, bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id, and rule { status="Enabled"; destination { bucket=aws_s3_bucket.replica.arn } }.
justification: Cross-region replication improves durability and disaster recovery. See AWS S3 replication documentation.

title: Ensure all data stored in the S3 bucket have versioning enabled
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_versioning "public_assets" { bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id; versioning_configuration { status="Enabled" } }.
justification: Versioning protects against accidental deletion and overwrite. See AWS S3 versioning documentation.

title: Ensure the S3 bucket has access logging enabled
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_logging "public_assets" { bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id; target_bucket=var.log_bucket_id; target_prefix="log/" }.
justification: Access logging provides audit trails for S3 requests. See AWS S3 server access logging documentation.

title: Ensure that an S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration
proposed_fix: Add aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration "public_assets" { bucket=aws_s3_bucket.public_assets.id; rule { id="expire"; status="Enabled"; expiration { days=365 } } }.
justification: Lifecycle rules manage retention and reduce stale data risk. See AWS S3 lifecycle configuration documentation.

title: Ensure AWS IAM policy does not allow full IAM privileges
proposed_fix: Remove iam:* and full-admin permissions; replace with explicit required actions on specific resources, e.g. Action=["s3:GetObject"], Resource=["arn:aws:s3:::demo-public-assets-example-llmsec/*"].
justification: Full IAM privileges allow account takeover. Use least privilege per AWS IAM best practices.

title: Minimize the admission of root containers
proposed_fix: Add securityContext: runAsNonRoot=true; runAsUser=10000; and remove privileged/root execution for container web.
justification: Running as non-root reduces container breakout impact. See Kubernetes security context and Pod Security Standards.

title: Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary
proposed_fix: Add automountServiceAccountToken=false under spec.template.spec unless the pod explicitly needs Kubernetes API access.
justification: Disabling automatic token mounting reduces credential exposure. See Kubernetes service account token documentation.

title: Apply security context to your pods and containers
proposed_fix: Add securityContext at pod and container levels: runAsNonRoot=true; runAsUser=10000; privileged=false; allowPrivilegeEscalation=false; readOnlyRootFilesystem=true; capabilities.drop=["ALL"].
justification: Explicit security contexts enforce least privilege. See Kubernetes security context documentation.

title: Memory requests should be set
proposed_fix: Add resources.requests.memory to container web, e.g. resources: requests: { cpu: "100m"; memory: "128Mi" }.
justification: Memory requests aid scheduling and prevent resource starvation. See Kubernetes resource management documentation.

title: The default namespace should not be used
proposed_fix: Add metadata.namespace: demo to the Deployment and create/use a non-default namespace for the workload.
justification: Avoiding the default namespace improves isolation and policy control. See Kubernetes namespace documentation.

title: Containers should run as a high UID to avoid host conflict
proposed_fix: Set securityContext.runAsUser: 10000 and runAsNonRoot: true for container web.
justification: High UIDs avoid collisions with host users. See Kubernetes security context and Pod Security Standards.

title: Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned
proposed_fix: Add securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] to container web, and add back only explicitly required capabilities.
justification: Dropping Linux capabilities reduces privilege. See Kubernetes capabilities and Pod Security Standards.

title: Ensure that the seccomp profile is set to docker/default or runtime/default
proposed_fix: Add securityContext.seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault } at pod or container level.
justification: Seccomp restricts syscalls and reduces kernel attack surface. See Kubernetes seccomp documentation.

title: Memory limits should be set
proposed_fix: Add resources.limits.memory to container web, e.g. resources: limits: { cpu: "500m"; memory: "256Mi" }.
justification: Memory limits prevent runaway resource consumption. See Kubernetes resource management documentation.

title: Image should use digest
proposed_fix: Pin image by digest, e.g. image: nginx@sha256:<verified-digest> instead of nginx:latest.
justification: Digest pinning ensures immutable image deployment. See Kubernetes image documentation.

title: Image Tag should be fixed - not latest or blank
proposed_fix: Replace image: nginx:latest with a fixed version tag, e.g. image: nginx:1.27.0.
justification: Fixed tags avoid unpredictable updates. See Kubernetes image best practices.

title: Container should not be privileged
proposed_fix: Change securityContext.privileged from true to false for container web, and remove unnecessary privileged capabilities.
justification: Privileged containers can escape isolation. See Kubernetes security context and Pod Security Standards.

title: Readiness Probe Should be Configured
proposed_fix: Add readinessProbe to container web, e.g. readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /; port: 80 }; initialDelaySeconds: 5 }.
justification: Readiness probes prevent routing to unhealthy pods. See Kubernetes probes documentation.

title: Containers should not run with allowPrivilegeEscalation
proposed_fix: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false for container web.
justification: Disabling privilege escalation prevents setuid/setgid escalation. See Kubernetes security context documentation.

title: CPU limits should be set
proposed_fix: Add resources.limits.cpu to container web, e.g. resources: limits: { cpu: "500m"; memory: "256Mi" }.
justification: CPU limits prevent noisy-neighbor resource exhaustion. See Kubernetes resource management documentation.

title: Use read-only filesystem for containers where possible
proposed_fix: Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true for container web and mount writable volumes only where required.
justification: Read-only root filesystems reduce runtime tampering. See Kubernetes security context documentation.

title: Liveness Probe Should be Configured
proposed_fix: Add livenessProbe to container web, e.g. livenessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /; port: 80 }; initialDelaySeconds: 10 }.
justification: Liveness probes restart unhealthy containers. See Kubernetes probes documentation.

title: Minimize the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability
proposed_fix: Add securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["NET_RAW"] or ["ALL"] to container web.
justification: Dropping NET_RAW reduces network spoofing risk. See Kubernetes capabilities and Pod Security Standards.

title: CPU requests should be set
proposed_fix: Add resources.requests.cpu to container web, e.g. resources: requests: { cpu: "100m"; memory: "128Mi" }.
justification: CPU requests aid scheduling and capacity planning. See Kubernetes resource management documentation.

title: Minimize the admission of pods which lack an associated NetworkPolicy
proposed_fix: Create a NetworkPolicy selecting app: demo with policyTypes [Ingress, Egress] and explicit allowed ingress/egress rules.
justification: NetworkPolicies restrict pod traffic and reduce lateral movement. See Kubernetes NetworkPolicy documentation.

title: Ensure the base image uses a non latest version tag
proposed_fix: Replace FROM ubuntu:latest with FROM ubuntu:22.04 or a pinned digest, e.g. FROM ubuntu:22.04@sha256:<digest>.
justification: Pinned base images make builds reproducible and avoid unexpected changes. See Docker image best practices.

title: Ensure the last USER is not root
proposed_fix: Replace USER root with a non-root user, e.g. RUN useradd -u 10001 appuser && USER appuser.
justification: Running as non-root reduces container compromise impact. See Docker USER instruction and CIS Docker Benchmark.

title: Ensure that HEALTHCHECK instructions have been added to container images
proposed_fix: Add HEALTHCHECK, e.g. HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost/ || exit 1.
justification: Health checks let orchestrators detect unhealthy containers. See Docker HEALTHCHECK documentation.

title: Avoid 'latest' tag; pin a digest or version.
proposed_fix: Replace FROM ubuntu:latest with FROM ubuntu:22.04 or FROM ubuntu:22.04@sha256:<digest>.
justification: Avoiding latest prevents non-reproducible builds and unexpected base image changes. See Docker image tagging best practices.

title: Kubernetes container should not run privileged.
proposed_fix: Set securityContext.privileged: false for container web and remove privileged capabilities.
justification: Privileged containers can compromise the node. See Kubernetes Pod Security Standards and security context documentation.
